title: DriveDreamer4D: World Models Are Effective Data Machines for 4D Driving Scene Representation

output_modality.value: Single (front) view driving video of novel trajectories, used as extra data to train 4D Gaussian Splatting scene representations.

control_signal.value: Edited ego actions (steering angle, speed) give a novel trajectory, from which 3D box sequences and HD map sequences are extracted; also first frame and text prompt.

control_mechanism.value: Structured conditions (3D boxes, HDMap, text) are fed as control inputs to a controllable video diffusion model; conditions are view-projected in sync with the maneuver.

base_model.value: Video diffusion world model following [81], initialised from SVD, front view only, 40 frames at 960 x 640; videos then optimise PVG, S3Gaussian or Deformable-GS 4DGS baselines.

datasets.value: Waymo: full training split (798 videos, about 64K 40-frame clips) for the generator; eight selected validation scenes for evaluation.

metrics.value: FID on novel-trajectory renderings, proposed NTA-IoU (agents) and NTL-IoU (lanes), and a user study win rate.

controllability_evidence.value: Novel-trajectory renderings are checked with NTA-IoU and FID: average NTA-IoU improves by 22.6%, 43.5% and 15.6% over the three baselines; lane-change FID for PVG falls from 105.29 to 71.52.

closed_loop.value: No; novel-trajectory videos are rendered and scored offline. The paper only positions the method as a foundation for closed-loop simulation.

notes: The world model is a data generator for 4DGS reconstruction rather than the end product, and control is via trajectory edits turned into box and map conditions. Control mechanism details are partial in the packet.
